name: Ramsay MacDonald
role: British prime minister (1924, 1929–1935), first Labour premier and leader of the National Government
summary: Ramsay MacDonald was a gradualist parliamentary socialist of the Independent Labour Party who rejected class war, economic determinism, syndicalism and the dictatorship of the proletariat, and held that property is justified only by social service. He opposed Britain's role in the First World War, led two Labour minority governments, and in 1931 formed the cross-party National Government, which split his party.

notes: First audit. Read by theme from his own books on archive.org: Parliament and Revolution (1919), The Socialist Movement (1911), Socialism: Critical and Constructive (1921), Syndicalism (1912). A Policy for the Labour Party (1920) was read for foreign policy and Ireland. Labour and the Empire (1907), Socialism and Government (1909) and the conclusion and index of The Government of India (1919) were read for empire, race, church and state. Not read through: the body of The Government of India, Socialism and Society (1905), the 1903 Zollverein book beyond its foreword, conclusion and chapter on the colonies, and A Socialist in Palestine (1922). Hansard (UK Commons speeches as prime minister, 1932-35) was searched for tariffs, the means test, India, disarmament and the League of Nations; his statements there describe government business and settle none of the statements, so his tariff answers rest on the record of the government he led (import duty orders 1932-35, announced by him), which governs over his 1903-1907 writings against protection; both are kept in the source list and the answers are low. His 1931 break with the Labour Party is a change of party, not of the views in the books. Economy, foreign and cultural statements are mostly null.
